tables.title: Top-down vs. bottom-up
rows: Sensory receptors register information and send it up to the brain
Being aware of the squiggles in a handwritten note
Knowledge, experience, or context interprets what you sense
Knowing what the squiggles mean; reading scrambled words

tables.title: Thresholds
rows: The weakest stimulus you can detect 50% of the time
A watch ticking 20 feet away; 1 teaspoon of salt in 2 gallons of water
The smallest change you notice 50% of the time
Car music from 5 to 6: probably not noticed. From 5 to 10: probably noticed
Changes must be a constant percentage, not a constant amount
1 oz added to 10 oz is noticed; 1 oz added to 100 oz isn't. Weight must change 2%

cheat.title: Attention
items: Change blindness = missing a change. Inattentional blindness = missing an object entirely. Both: attention is elsewhere.
Cocktail party effect: hearing your name in a noisy room. Pop-out: the one odd item jumps out.

cheat.title: Processing
items: Bottom-up = senses up to the brain (sensation).

cheat.title: Thresholds
items: Absolute threshold = weakest stimulus detected 50% of the time.
Difference threshold (JND) = smallest change noticed 50% of the time.
Weber's law: a constant percentage, not a constant amount (weight: about 2%).

cheat.title: ESP
items: Telepathy, clairvoyance, precognition: no scientific basis.
Psychics seem accurate because people remember hits and forget misses.
